ABOUT THIS SANDBOX

A small, hands-on
robotics workbench.

This demo is an interactive illustration, not an experiment from the paper. There is no trained Sim2Real-RL policy in this file.

Robot and gripper

Seven-joint origins, axes and limits follow the inspected RM75-B configuration, including the flange spacer. The white curved casings are dimensioned reconstructions, not imported manufacturer CAD. The gripper follows an opposing-linkage geometry with articulated levers, pivots and parallel finger supports. Visual screws and shell details are illustrative.

Physical stacking, within a small model

Both 50 mm cubes are dynamic: the lower cube can move too. Contact impulses, friction and gravity govern their motion. Fingers follow the linkage arc. Neither cube is snapped, welded or attached to the gripper or to the other cube. Contact shapes are simplified boxes; the arm has kinematic servos and no full dynamics or self-collision. This is a custom solver, not MuJoCo and not a hardware controller.

Random layouts and success

New layout randomizes the starting positions of both A and B; Reset replays the same layout. B is the target and stays wherever physics moves it. Success requires A to be released on B, aligned within 10 mm, near the correct height, upright and quiet for 1.2 seconds after the fingers withdraw. These are demo settings, not paper evaluation thresholds.

Manual vs scripted

Manual commands move a downward-facing grasp frame through inverse kinematics. The scripted example reads both simulated cube positions and follows programmed waypoints. It does not run a trained Sim2Real-RL policy. Manual controls interrupt the script.

Local operation

Meshes, rendering and simulation are embedded in this file. It makes no network request and has no external fonts, analytics, policy download or robot connection. Hosting providers may maintain access logs.
